edition: August Dillmann, Lexicon linguae Aethiopicae cum indice latino, Leipzig: Th.O. Weigel,1865

findings.entry_qualification: Dillmann prints alternate segmentation (an ተልሕየ?) and III,1; retain uncertainty in perfect lemma, not a guessed new lexeme.
findings.observed_passage_citation: Hen.39,7, with selected Ethiopic quoted fire-light clause, including ይትለሐዩ.
findings.morphological_analysis: The quoted finite form ይትለሐዩ is plural imperfect (third-person masculine plural in the clause) of the III,1 reflexive formation cited by Dillmann. The preceding righteous/chosen are the plural subject.
findings.source_glyph_finding: Charles1906 printed79 word enlargement is consistent with ይትለሐዩ, not submitted ይትሰሐዩ; propose correction of third glyph ሰ to ለ, contingent on independent exact-scan confirmation. The lexicon quote is not substituted for the selected Charles text.
findings.proposed_english_fragment: All the righteous and chosen shine before him like the light of fire.
findings.proposed_footnote: Dillmann1865 col33 cites this verse under a reflexive verb meaning to adorn oneself/be radiant; the alternate perfect-form segmentation in that entry is uncertain. Charles records differing verbal readings in printed79 note20; this follows the selected printed line.
findings.limits: Lexical equivalence now has direct primary support, not just the fire simile. This does not independently prove every manuscript or remove need to confirm the source glyph correction.

observed_latin_glosses: confugere in locum vel ad aliquem
precibus vel auxilium petendo adire aliquem
findings.observed_passage_citation: c.Acc.Hen.45,3, explicitly under sense1 prayer/refuge/appeal before separate sense2 queri/incusare/criminari.
findings.morphological_analysis: ሰከዩ is perfect third-person masculine plural of ሰከየ, with the relative እለ yielding those who have called upon/appealed to. The following name phrase is the accusative construction specifically cited in the primary lexicon.
findings.proposed_english_fragment: and those who have called upon my glorious name.
findings.proposed_footnote: Dillmann1865 col383 cites45:3 under approaching someone in prayer or seeking aid. The distinct accusation sense is not selected here.
findings.limits: Supports invocation/appeal without identifying an unstated liturgical rite or importing a later English translation. Does not remove the independent corruption dagger earlier in45:3.
